issues.description: Output-response bookend invariant can be violated by overlapping invocations.
issues.detail: The contract claims an LLMFullResponseStartFrame is paired with an EndFrame. But if a second LLMContextFrame arrives while _close_task is pending or while the first invocation is still streaming, _output_response_open and _close_task are shared mutable state with no lock. Concurrent _push_text_frame calls can interleave Start/End frames or drop the End entirely. State the invariant and serialize access.

issues.description: Transformer contract under-specified: exceptions and partial payloads leak implementation.
issues.detail: default_response_to_output_transformer calls json.loads with no try/except, so a malformed line raises and aborts the whole stream mid-response, leaving _output_response_open true and bookends unbalanced. The transformer's contract (must it return None on parse failure? may it raise?) is not stated. Define the precondition/postcondition for both transformers and handle violations at the boundary.

issues.description: LSP violation risk: LLMContext and OpenAILLMContext treated as substitutable but aren't.
issues.detail: default_context_to_payload_transformer calls last_message.get('role') and isinstance(last_message, LLMSpecificMessage). This assumes messages are dict-like across both context types. If OpenAILLMContext or future LLMContext subtypes return non-dict message objects, the precondition silently fails (returns None) rather than surfacing the type mismatch. The supertype contract for context.messages needs to be stated.

issues.description: Module boundary leaks AWS client lifecycle into per-frame processing.
issues.detail: A new bedrock-agentcore client is opened and torn down on every LLMContextFrame. The processor's abstract responsibility is 'invoke an agent and emit text frames'; client lifecycle belongs to the module's setup/teardown, not its per-call hot path. This leaks aioboto3 session semantics through the operation contract and adds per-frame latency. Open the client once in setup() and close it in cleanup().

issues.description: Naming violates the module's stated naming convention (agentArn).
issues.detail: The constructor parameter agentArn uses camelCase while all sibling parameters use snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region). The PEP 8 contract for Python public APIs is snake_case; mixing breaks substitutability with other Pipecat processors that callers configure uniformly. Rename to agent_arn (the AWS field name agentRuntimeArn can remain at the boto3 boundary).

issues.description: Class name in code (AWSAgentCoreProcessor) differs from PR title (AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor).
issues.detail: The PR title and the exported class name disagree. This is a small spec-vs-implementation drift, but for a public processor name it matters: callers import by name and the name is part of the contract. Pick one and use it in docstring, class, and PR.

review.summary: The processor's abstract data type is reasonable: take an LLMContext, produce LLMTextFrames bracketed by Start/End bookends. But the contract is under-stated in several places where it matters. The Start/End invariant is held by mutable instance state with no serialization, so overlapping invocations can break the bookend pairing. The transformer interfaces don't specify behavior under malformed input, and the default response transformer will raise on bad JSON mid-stream, leaving the response open. The AWS client lifecycle leaks into the per-frame path. Naming inconsistencies (agentArn, class-name vs PR title) are small but real spec drift.
